definition: The five-factor personality model is a way of describing personality in terms of five broad trait dimensions. In this packet, it is presented as a framework that closely aligns with dimensional measures of maladaptive personality traits and helps describe personality pathology and its links to personality disorders.

reasons: The packet supports the five-factor model’s relevance to personality pathology and personality disorder prediction, but it does not explicitly define the model as a way of describing personality in terms of five broad trait dimensions.

The definition overstates the packet by presenting the five-factor personality model as closely aligning with dimensional maladaptive-trait measures as a defining feature, rather than as a contextual alignment shown for specific instruments in this article.

The packet does not explicitly state that the five-factor personality model is “describing personality in terms of five broad trait dimensions”; it only refers to the “five-factor personality model/FFM” in relation to other measures without clearly defining those five dimensions within the provided text.

The definition’s phrase “dimensional measures of maladaptive personality traits” is not directly supported as written; the packet discusses “personality pathology” and five pathological domains, but it does not specifically describe these as “maladaptive personality traits” in the same terms.
